findings: Launcher started codex exec with workspace-write sandbox and emitted an ACK.
The delegated session failed before repository inspection with bwrap loopback RTM_NEWADDR Operation not permitted.
No tests, lint, build, or smoke commands ran.
interpretations: The nested workspace-write sandbox is incompatible with the current execution environment.
Retry requires a launcher-level sandbox compatibility change or an environment capability change.
limitations: The Intake Agent collected no repository design evidence and produced no recommendation.

findings: Human review occurs after Workflow Agent Report and has exactly rework or complete outcomes.
For worktree mode, complete triggers automatic integration into local factory; no push or promotion follows.
Rework records the exact instruction, reuses the same background Goal path, increments revision, and invalidates prior outcomes.
Completed worktrees remain until later batch cleanup, which refuses dirty worktrees.
interpretations: The current complete decision couples Human acceptance and factory integration, leaving no canonical reviewed-but-not-integrated state.
The retained worktree supports later inspection but its internal path is not suitable as a Human-facing interface.
limitations: Documents specify intended behavior; runtime behavior was not exercised.

findings: worktree.py exposes internal prepare, inspect, integrate, cleanup, and cleanup-completed commands; inspect returns branch, changes, headCommit, repository, and absolute worktreePath.
work_unit.py status summarizes lifecycleStatus, executionState, reviewStatus, integrationResult, and validationStatus.

rework-start is accepted only from review, requires an instruction, archives the current attempt, increments currentRevision, resets attempt identity and progress, and returns the Work Unit to working.
transition to done requires review-decision complete; done validation requires a complete human-review-result bound to the current execution target.
app_server_goal.py starts the Workflow Agent at the primary repository cwd and emits machine-oriented ACK and terminal payloads containing repository and canonical package paths.
interpretations: Existing managers provide most backend primitives for a facade, but their raw JSON contracts leak implementation paths and are not a Human review presentation model.
A review facade can derive stable public identity from Work Unit id and manager status while keeping paths, script names, commits, branches, and protocol payloads behind an adapter.
limitations: No command was executed beyond read-only source inspection; output formatting and Codex client rendering were not observed.

findings: README documents installation, lifecycle framing, development validation, and test authority, but no Human review command or UI.
plugin.json provides one natural-language defaultPrompt to inspect the project and route the next lifecycle action.
Skill UI metadata exposes default prompts for lifecycle, agents, intakes, and work-units; the repository contains no plugin command directory or dedicated review application entry point.
interpretations: The lowest-cost user entry point is a conversational lifecycle intent backed by a presentation adapter; a dedicated local web view is a later extension.
Publishing direct manager commands would conflict with the goal of hiding internal skills scripts and long worktree paths.
limitations: The installed Codex host UI and any capabilities outside this repository were not inspected.
